leader.headline: Schaeffler's share-price drop on disappointing earnings demands immediate buyer attention, while Knorr-Bremse and Hitachi Energy advance positive capacity investments that lower long-term risk.
leader.summary_md: The portfolio shows five suppliers all at Medium risk (scores 30.8–38.0), three of them High-criticality (Knorr-Bremse, Schaeffler, Hitachi Energy). Over the past week the only material negative signal came from Schaeffler: shares fell to a 12‑month low after quarterly results were described as disappointing, pushing its Geopolitics & Reputation area score to 44.7 despite Q3 results within guidance and a completed cost‑reduction program. Knorr-Bremse posted a cluster of positive developments – first revenue service of its digital electromechanical brake in Italy, a strategic MoU with China’s railway academy, ambitious €10bn/16% margin targets, and a Moody’s A3 stable affirmation – which together drove its score down 2.3 points. Hitachi Energy announced two major North American investments (C$479M in Ontario, $528M in Mississippi) that will strengthen traction‑transformer supply resilience over time. Hübner Group’s only event was a republished 2022 report on a new Hungarian elastomer plant; Voith had no relevant news. **Next steps:** 1) Engage Schaeffler management to clarify the earnings trajectory and confirm axlebox‑bearing delivery schedules. 2) Verify whether European freight weakness flagged by Jefferies affects Knorr-Bremse’s braking‑system order book. 3) Track milestone progress of Hitachi’s Ontario insulation factory and Mississippi plant for traction‑transformer supply assurance.

watchlist.reason: Shares hit 12-month low after disappointing quarterly results, raising market confidence concerns despite Q3 results within guidance and cost program completion.
watchlist.action: Engage Schaeffler management to clarify earnings trajectory and monitor axlebox bearing delivery schedules.
